transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

The 4C code on your Samsung DW60M6050FS typically indicates a water supply issue, meaning the dishwasher isn't receiving enough fresh water to start or continue its cycle. This is often caused by a closed water tap, a kinked inlet hose, or a clogged filter at the connection point. Before we look further, please ensure the water tap behind the machine is fully open and check that the small mesh filter on the inlet hose isn't blocked with sand or debris. If the tap is on and the filter looks clear, let me know and we can check if the drain hose might be blocking the cycle.
Ok. There's a screwdriver-slot valve under the sink for the dishwasher and it's turned at 90 degrees, so I think it's off. A plumber fitted a new tap yesterday. Should I turn it on?

Yes, please turn that screwdriver-slot valve fully on so it is parallel with the pipe (that is the 'open' position). Once it is open, try starting a cycle again. If the machine starts filling and the error clears, you are good to go. If the 4C code persists even with the tap open, we will need to check if the inlet hose filter at the back of the dishwasher is blocked by debris from the new installation.
Done, I've turned the valve so it's parallel with the pipe and started a cycle. It's filling and running normally now, no 4C.

That’s excellent news. The 4C code was simply because the isolation valve under the sink was closed after the plumber's visit. Since it is now running normally, you can leave that valve in the parallel (open) position for future use. If you have any other questions or if anything else comes up with your dishwasher, just let me know.

candidates: Water supply issue (clogged inlet filter or closed tap) (high)
Kinked or blocked drain hose preventing cycle start (medium)
